claims.claim: Exactly-once entitlement grant is enforced via a unique constraint on order_id inside the payment-confirmation transaction.
claims.evidence: Data storage (line 61) and AD-03 (line 166) describe a unique constraint on order_id in the entitlements table within the payment txn; CAP-07 mapping row repeats it.

claims.claim: No double-sale of license keys is guaranteed via SELECT ... FOR UPDATE SKIP LOCKED / status CAS plus a Redis reservation gate.
claims.evidence: Data storage (line 61), Cache (line 65-66), and AD-04 (line 171) describe the Redis reservation + Postgres SKIP LOCKED/CAS two-layer approach.

suggestions.assertion: Each tech stack layer gives a Recommendation, a Why/rationale, and at least one Alternative
suggestions.reason: Third-party services and Security layers are itemized lists rather than the Recommendation/Why/Alternative triplet. The check passes on core layers; specifying which layers must carry the full triplet would make it more discriminating.

This run added a license-key storage layer and detailed exactly-once / no-oversell concurrency controls that exceed the other runs — strong correctness depth that no assertion rewards. An assertion checking that finite-inventory/license-key concurrency is addressed would credit genuine digital-goods correctness and discriminate stronger from weaker outputs.

eval_feedback.overall: Assertions are comprehensive and align with OUTPUT_FORMAT. They reliably pass for a correct output; consider one content assertion for digital-goods-specific correctness (exactly-once entitlement / license-key oversell) to reward the depth this run demonstrated.
